sentences.text: Heteroptychodus was an extinct hybodont shark that possessed low, rounded teeth designed for crushing hard objects, which were covered in ridges.
Fossils of this genus have been recovered from freshwater environments, a surprising habitat for a shark.
The genus Heteroptychodus was described by Yabe and Obata in 1930.
Its specialized dentition suggests a diet focused on hard-shelled prey, though the exact hunting strategies remain unknown.
Heteroptychodus is a member of the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish, and belongs to the family Hybodontidae and the subfamily Hybodontinae.
The genus lived from the Tithonian to the Albian stages, between 149.2 and 100.5 million years ago, with fossils found in Japan, Mongolia, Malaysia, Thailand, Southern China, and possibly Kyrgyzstan.
